title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.

output.observation: This is the StoryHearth landing page, introducing a service that creates illustrated family storybooks from a child, another character, and a shared memory. The page offers prominent “Proceed” and “See pricing” buttons, explains a three-step process, and includes a log-in link.
output.think_aloud: This looks relevant to me, although “multimodal generative narrative engine” and “lived-experience corpus” sound far more technical and grand than making a bedtime story. The simple three steps and mention of a free digital preview make me curious, so I’ll log in first.

site_model.what_it_is: A website for generating personalised, illustrated family storybooks from supplied family details and a memory.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting a story starring their child and another loved one, apparently with a reading age suited to young children.
site_model.value_proposition: Turn a meaningful family memory into an illustrated storybook, with a free digital preview and an option for printed hardcovers.
main_tasks: Add the child and another character
Describe a place, treasured object, and memory
Generate and read the illustrated storybook
Check the price of a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: The digital preview is free; printed hardcovers are available, but no actual price is shown on this page.
trust_signals: A claim that the preview is free
Testimonials attributed to named customers and UK cities
site_model.fit_for_me: It sounds well suited to making a keepsake story about Sam and Grandpa Joe, provided the writing and pictures are genuinely child-friendly.

page_review.purpose: Explain the personalised family-storybook service and direct visitors to creation, pricing, or account access.
page_review.what_is_happening: The landing page presents the service proposition, two calls to action, a three-step overview, testimonials, FAQs, and legal/contact links. No story or other generated content is present yet.
page_review.first_impression: It looks warm and polished, but the main paragraph is unnecessarily technical and pretentious for what is essentially a children’s story service.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I want to log in and make the book.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the “Log in” button is clearly visible in the top-right corner.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Log in” is direct and familiar.

issues.title: The main description uses confusing technical language
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Most of that sentence is jargon and sounds like marketing aimed at technology experts rather than parents. It makes the service harder to understand at first glance.
issues.fix: Replace it with plain language, such as: “Turn a special family memory into a personalised, illustrated storybook starring your loved ones.”

issues.title: Decorative image has no description
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The large illustration may be unavailable or unexplained to someone using a screen reader.
issues.fix: Add meaningful alt text describing the image, or mark it decorative with an empty alt attribute if it adds no information.

positives: The “How it works” section gives a clear three-step overview.
The call to action to get a free digital preview is reassuring.
The page has clear navigation to pricing and login.
The visual style feels warm and family-friendly.

output.memory_note: The digital preview is advertised as free; no hardcover price is shown on the landing page.
output.plan: I’ll use the visible “Log in” control and sign in with the provided account details.

page_review.purpose: Show the books in my account and provide a way to create a new one.
page_review.what_is_happening: After login, the page says “Welcome back, Demo” and “You have no books yet.” A prominent button offers to create a new book, while a technical error alert reports that profile sync is incomplete.
page_review.first_impression: The page is simple and the next step is easy to find, but the error code at the top looks like something has gone wrong and gives me no idea whether it matters.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try creating the new book because this is exactly what I came to do.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the orange “+ Create a new book” button is prominent and easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Create a new book” clearly matches what I want to do.

issues.title: Technical error code shown without an explanation
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes me wonder whether my account or story information has not loaded correctly, even though I can still continue.
issues.fix: Replace the error code with a plain-language message such as “We couldn’t finish syncing your profile. You can still create a book,” and add a “Try again” button if retrying is useful.

issues.title: Error has no recovery guidance
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am not told whether the problem is temporary, serious, or safe to ignore.
issues.fix: State whether the account is still usable and provide either an automatic retry or a clear support/retry action.

issues.title: Footer links are barely visible
issues.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear in very faint grey text.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The links are difficult to read, especially the contact link that could be useful if something goes wrong.
issues.fix: Use a darker, higher-contrast text colour while retaining normal link affordances.

positives: The page clearly confirms that I am logged in with “Welcome back, Demo.”
The empty-book state is concise and easy to understand.
The primary “+ Create a new book” action is visually prominent and clearly labelled.

title: Your storybook – StoryHearth

output.observation: The generated nine-page storybook preview is open at the cover, titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam.” The cover shows a simple Sam illustration, and navigation arrows let me move through the book; pricing and order options are farther down the page.
output.think_aloud: It did generate the book, so that worked, but the title has a typo: “Adventrue.” I also asked for the soft watercolour style, yet the page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic” and the cover is extremely plain rather than looking like my memory.
output.last_action_feedback: yes — the new preview, title, page count, and 1 / 9 indicator clearly show that the book was created.

page_review.purpose: Preview the newly generated nine-page personalised storybook and offer regeneration and hardcover ordering.
page_review.what_is_happening: The first of nine pages is displayed as a book cover. The story is titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam,” and the output claims a Pop-art comic illustration style. A next arrow is available, while regeneration and ordering controls are below the fold.
page_review.first_impression: The book appeared and the cover is readable, but the misspelled title immediately makes it feel unfinished. The style also does not match the watercolour choice I made, and the generic sun-and-character image is disappointing for a family memory.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I need to read all nine pages carefully before deciding whether the result is good enough to order.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the right arrow labelled “›” is visible beneath the cover and the page indicator says 1 / 9.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Partly. The arrow indicates moving to the next page, but it is a symbol rather than a clearly written “Next page” control.

issues.title: Generated title contains an obvious spelling error
issues.evidence: The heading and cover both say “The Magical Adventrue of Sam.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The title is prominent on the cover, so the typo makes the finished book look careless and not ready to print.
issues.fix: Spell-check generated titles before showing them, and let me edit the title or regenerate just that text without paying.

issues.title: The generated style contradicts my selected style
issues.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” although I selected the soft watercolour style.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I made a deliberate choice about the look, so paying for a different style would feel misleading.
issues.fix: Use the selected style consistently and display the exact saved choice before generation; if it cannot be honoured, explain why before payment.

issues.title: The cover does not reflect the supplied family memory
issues.evidence: The cover is a generic character under a sun with “A StoryHearth original,” and no beach, Grandpa Joe, sandcastles, or yellow bucket is shown.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The promise is a personalised family memory, so a generic cover makes me question whether the story itself will remember the details I entered.
issues.fix: Use the entered people, beach setting, sandcastles, and yellow bucket in the cover, or clearly label it as a placeholder if a memory-specific cover is unavailable.

issues.title: Book navigation uses an unlabelled symbol
issues.evidence: The only forward control is the button labelled “›,” with no visible “Next page” text.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can guess what it does, but the spoken name may simply be “greater than,” which is not clear for assistive technology.
issues.fix: Give the control an accessible name such as “Next page” and retain a visible label if space allows.

positives: The creation result is unmistakable, with a title, cover, and 1 / 9 page indicator.
The generated cover and title are large and easy to see.
The page counter helps me understand that there are eight more pages to read.

output.output_reaction: I’m disappointed and suspicious that the site ignored my watercolour choice. “Adventrue” is spelled wrong, and the cover is so generic that I do not yet believe Grandpa Joe, the beach, the sandcastles, or the yellow bucket will actually appear.
output.memory_note: The generated book has 9 pages; its title is “The Magical Adventrue of Sam,” and it unexpectedly says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic.” Regeneration is listed as $4.99.
output.plan: I’ll use the next-page arrow and read every page carefully, looking for Sam, Grandpa Joe, the beach, the sandcastles, the yellow bucket, age-appropriate language, and other mistakes before checking the hardcover cost.

output.observation: The checkout shows a £24.99 hardcover, £12.99 shipping, a pre-selected £7.99 premium gift wrap, and a total of £45.97. A countdown says the price is reserved for 09:57, and address and payment fields are visible, but I will not enter payment or bank details.
output.think_aloud: The basic hardcover costs £24.99, but I nearly assumed the full price was £45.97 because “Premium gift wrap” is already ticked. I don’t want that extra, so I’ll untick it and see the real total before stopping without paying.
output.last_action_feedback: yes — clicking “Order hardcover” clearly took me to Checkout and showed the hardcover price and full order breakdown.

page_review.purpose: To show the cost of ordering the generated book as a hardcover and collect delivery and payment information.
page_review.what_is_happening: The checkout prices The Magical Adventrue of Sam at £24.99, adds £12.99 shipping, and pre-selects £7.99 premium gift wrap, making the current total £45.97. The page also shows a 09:57 price-reservation countdown, address fields, card fields, and a Pay now button below the fold.
page_review.first_impression: The order summary is easy to read, but the pre-ticked gift wrap feels sneaky because it adds £7.99 without me asking. The countdown also feels like unnecessary pressure.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would untick “Premium gift wrap” to find the actual cost of the hardcover without the unwanted extra.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the checked “Premium gift wrap” checkbox with [6] is visible beside the £7.99 charge.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Premium gift wrap” clearly identifies the extra, although the fact that it is pre-selected does not match what I want.

issues.title: Gift wrap is pre-selected without being requested
issues.evidence: Checkbox [6] “Premium gift wrap” is checked, with “£7.99” shown.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes the total £45.97 instead of the £37.98 I would expect for the hardcover and shipping, so I could pay for something I did not choose.
issues.fix: Make optional extras unchecked by default and require an explicit choice to add them.

issues.title: Artificial reservation countdown creates pressure
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes me rush and could stop me from checking the price and order details carefully.
issues.fix: Remove the countdown unless the reservation genuinely has a firm, explained deadline, and state the exact deadline and conditions.

issues.title: The purchase is not framed as clearly optional
issues.evidence: [11] button “Pay now” appears below the fold after the address and card fields.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A clear “Return to preview” or “Back” option would make it easier to stop without buying.
issues.fix: Place an obvious cancel or return-to-preview link beside Pay now and preserve the book preview.

positives: The £24.99 hardcover price is shown plainly.
Shipping is shown separately as £12.99.
The total includes every currently selected charge.
page_review.abandon_reason: I would not pay because I have not requested premium gift wrap, and I will not enter card details. I will only remove the extra to establish the real cost.

output.memory_note: Hardcover £24.99; shipping £12.99; pre-ticked premium gift wrap £7.99; current total £45.97. Without gift wrap, the expected total is £37.98.
output.plan: Untick the pre-selected premium gift wrap, then read the updated total. I will stop there and not fill in the address or payment fields or press Pay now.
